claims.text: The dataset records 633 partner institutions across 50 countries. The map shows 266 partners with at least two shared papers, usable locations and no flagged affiliation match. It does not display every institution in the dataset. Counted by partner country, 36.5 percent of the collaboration is with US institutions and 28.2 percent with Chinese ones; the closing paragraph rounds these to 37 and 28 percent.
claims.source: OpenAlex works 2015-2024 classified in subfield 2507 'Polymers and Plastics' with an Akron or Case Western authorship. A CLASSIFICATION, not the full-text keyword an earlier version used.
claims.assert: D['totals']['partners_shown'] == 629 and D['totals']['partners'] == 633 and D['totals']['countries'] == 50 and len(D['map']) == 266 and min(m['t'] for m in D['map']) == 2 and D['countries'][0]['code'] == 'US' and D['totals']['us_share'] == D['countries'][0]['share'] and int(D['totals']['us_share'] * 100 + 0.5) == 37 and int(one(c for c in D['countries'] if c['code'] == 'CN')['share'] * 100 + 0.5) == 28 and round(D['totals']['us_share'] * 100, 1) == 36.5 and round(one(c for c in D['countries'] if c['code'] == 'CN')['share'] * 100, 1) == 28.2 and (lambda M, T: T == 1545 and all(round(c['n'] / T, 4) == c['share'] for c in D['countries']) and all(c['n'] >= sum(m['t'] for m in M if m['c'] == c['code']) for c in D['countries']) and sum(c['n'] - sum(m['t'] for m in M if m['c'] == c['code']) for c in D['countries']) <= D['totals']['partners_shown'] - len(M))(D['map'], sum(m['t'] for m in D['map']) + D['totals']['partners_shown'] - len(D['map'])) and len({m['n'] for m in D['map']}) == len(D['map']) and all(any(m['n'] == p['name'] and m['c'] == p['country'] and m['l'] == p['led'] and m['j'] == p['joined'] and m['t'] == p['total'] for m in D['map']) for p in D['top']) and len(D['top']) == 40 and len({p['name'] for p in D['top']}) == 40 and all(D['top'][i]['total'] >= D['top'][i + 1]['total'] for i in range(39)) and all(m['lat'] is not None and m['lon'] is not None and -90 <= m['lat'] <= 90 and -180 <= m['lon'] <= 180 for m in D['map'])
claims.falsified_if: Either count moves. The bounds are pinned with == rather than > 500 and >= 40: the sentence says 600 institutions across 50 COUNTRIES and the old assert was satisfied by 40, so a page could have printed fifty while its data said forty and the board would have stayed green. An assert must be at least as strong as the sentence it certifies. This one caught a real error on 2026-08-31, in a slide deck that read the top-N country array's length as though it were the country total. Extended 2026-09-28 (round 4): the closer prints us_share and China's share; us_share disagreeing with the US row, or either rounding differently, fails it. The 37 is rounded half up, as the page's toFixed does; Python's round(36.5) gives 36. Round 5: the sentence prints one decimal, so 36.5 and 28.2 are pinned at one decimal too; and every shipped country share must be its count over one common total (at least the shown rows' sum), so a share cannot drift from the count beside it. China's whole percent is rounded half up too (Grok, round 5): Python's round(28.5) is 28 where the page's toFixed prints 29. [Round 6, 2026-09-28: searching for any denominator that fits the shares accepted a US count of 365 against 451 US partner-papers on the unchanged map. The denominator is now derived, not searched: the map's 1,182 partner-papers plus one for each of the 363 shown partners off the map (fewer than two shared papers, or no location), 1,545 today. Every country's count must be at least its own partners' papers on the map, and the counts above the map may not exceed the off-map partners. An off-map partner with two or more papers would move the true denominator above this derivation and fail the claim; that is a re-pin, not a data error.] [Round 7, 2026-09-28: the derivation is not an assumption about off-map partners. derive_reach.py divides by the sum of every shown partner's papers, so shares that equal their counts over 1,545 pin that sum to 1,545, which is the map's 1,182 plus exactly one paper for each of the 363 off-map partners. What the derivation could not see was identity: renaming a map row, or copying one over another with the same country and count, left every sum intact (Codex). Map names must now be unique, and every one of the 40 ranked partners must appear on the map with the same country and the same led, joined and total counts. A ranked partner losing its location would fail this; that is a re-pin.] [Round 8, 2026-09-28: the ranking is now forty distinct partners in descending order and every mapped partner carries a latitude and longitude in range (Codex, Grok). LIMIT: the 226 mapped partners outside the ranking have no second record to be checked against, so renaming one keeps every sum.]

claims.text: 985 of 1,222 papers naming a corresponding author had one here. That count includes papers with no outside co-author at all, not just papers won within a partnership. The page prints that share as 81%, from the stored led_share, which must equal 985 / 1,222 to four places.
claims.source: as above; is_corresponding, populated on about 84 percent of the corpus
claims.assert: D['totals']['led'] == 985 and D['totals']['joined'] == 237 and D['totals']['attributable'] == 1222 and D['totals']['no_corresponding'] == 226 and D['totals']['led_share'] == round(D['totals']['led'] / D['totals']['attributable'], 4) and D['totals']['joined_share'] == round(D['totals']['joined'] / D['totals']['attributable'], 4) and round(D['totals']['led_share'] * 100) == 81
claims.falsified_if: Any of the four counts moves. Pinned to exact values rather than a band, since 'led' is a raw tally of papers with a local corresponding author -- including papers with no outside institution -- and a rounded fraction like 'four in five' invited readers to assume it measured leadership within collaborations only. The 226 papers with no corresponding author flagged are excluded from the denominator and must stay excluded rather than assigned. Extended 2026-09-28 (round 4): the page prints led_share, not the counts, so a led_share that disagrees with led / attributable, or that rounds to anything but 81, fails it.

claims.text: 309 of the 1,364 papers with an OpenAlex citation-percentile score are in their field and year’s top tenth: 22.7 percent. The denominator is the scored subset of 1,448 collected works. The page prints it as 23% and the top hundredth as 2.4 percent, from stored shares that must equal those counts over 1,364.
claims.assert: D['totals']['top10'] == 309 and D['totals']['pct_n'] == 1364 and round(100 * D['totals']['top10'] / D['totals']['pct_n'], 1) == 22.7 and D['totals']['top10_share'] == round(D['totals']['top10'] / D['totals']['pct_n'], 4) and D['totals']['top1_share'] == round(D['totals']['top1'] / D['totals']['pct_n'], 4) and round(D['totals']['top10_share'] * 100) == 23 and tofixed(D['totals']['top1_share'] * 100, 1) == '2.4'
claims.falsified_if: Either the top-decile count or the number of scored papers changes; recompute the percentage from those counts rather than an already rounded share. Extended 2026-09-28 (round 4): the page prints the stored top10_share and top1_share, so either disagreeing with its count over pct_n fails it.

claims.text: The median paper sits just above the world average; the mean is 1.8 times it and is not the number to quote.
claims.falsified_if: The mean and median converge. Until they do, any summary using the mean describes a small tail and implies it describes the whole. The ratio is checked with tofixed, which rounds as the page's own toFixed(1) does, so the guard and the printed figure cannot straddle a rounding boundary.

claims.text: No raw citation count is compared across years anywhere on this page.
claims.falsified_if: Nothing in the data. A 2015 paper has had a decade to accumulate citations and a 2024 paper has had months, so a raw-citation trend draws the calendar rather than the research.

claims.text: Four institutions resolved implausibly by the affiliation parser are excluded, all four named, with their works reported and the one in China called out because this page publishes a country breakdown.
claims.assert: D['totals']['quarantined'] == 4 and len(D['quarantined']) == 4 and D['totals']['quarantined_works'] == 10 and sum(1 for q in D['quarantined'] if q['country'] == 'CN') == 1
claims.actual: [(q['name'], q['total'], q['why'][:60]) for q in D['quarantined']]
claims.falsified_if: The count of exclusions changes without the page changing with it. Pinned at four because the page reported ONE for as long as the code read quarantined[0] beside the typed word 'One', and an assert of >= 1 could not see the difference.

claims.text: Works are bounded by subject classification, not by matching the word 'polymer' in the text.
claims.source: OpenAlex subfield 2507, confirmed against the s3://openalex subfields snapshot rather than inferred
claims.falsified_if: The corpus grows back toward 4,000 works, which would mean the keyword bound has returned. The keyword put four hospitals in the five largest partners and healthcare institutions at 17 percent of the network; the classification puts them at 3.5 percent, because biomedical polymer work is a separate subfield (2502) and a keyword cannot tell the two apart.
